correctness.rationale: For F(x,y)=(y,ay−y³−bx), a≥0 and 0<b<1, all prime two cycles have coordinates (u,v)<->(v,u) satisfying B u=av−v³ and B v=au−u³, B=1+b. Factoring sum/difference gives either u=−v with u²=a+B (one antipodal saddle), u=v (fixed, excluded), or uv=B and u²+v²=a (exactly two sign-reversed non-antipodal cycles for a>2B). The return determinant is b²; trace for non-antipodal is −2a²+9B²−2b. Exact Jury inequalities give both sinks for 2B<a<sqrt((9B²+(1−b)²)/2), multipliers −1,−b² at equality, saddles above. Antipodal trace (−2a−3B)²−2b exceeds 1+b² for all specified parameters. Independent symbolic trace/threshold computations and sampled verifier review agree. The theorem is exhaustive for real prime-two orbits only, not other periods or nonlinear behavior at the flip.
